children: Amid rise in bond yields in the US, lowering capital gains will help in retaining investments by Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), said Anil Gupta, newly appointed President of industry chamber PHDCCI. He also called for further handholding of MSMEs and making land available at affordable cost to the industry for sustaining higher growth rate for Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Talking to businessline, Gupta, who is the Chairman & Managing Director of KEI wires and Cables, acknowledged that higher yield has been one of the factors for outflow of FII investment from stock market. “The yield in the US is 5.5 to 6 per cent, which is unprecedented. It is because of the high inflation in the US, and the Federal Reserve’s refusal to  reduce interest rates. When the interest rates are maintained at a very high level, bond yields are very high  there, but to stop the capital outflow from India, if the policies are investor friendly, the capital can be largely retained,” he said.

According to data from Central Depository Services Ltd (CDSL), though FPIs turned buyers towards end of last month, overall, they withdrew ₹34,843 crore from Indian equities in October, marking the second consecutive month of heavy outflows, amid concerns over elevated crude oil prices, global interest rates and the corporate earnings outlook. With the latest withdrawals, cumulative FPI outflows from Indian equities in 2026 have reached ₹2.95 lakh crore.

The industry chamber has submitted a representation to the Central Board of Direct Taxes for reviewing the capital gain tax. When asked what the response was, Gupta said, “Even if government wants to respond, they will not respond now. Budget is always a confidential thing. Whatever they will announce, that will come out in the budget. They will only listen to us and that’s all,” he said while refusing to speculate on market buzz about revision of taxes in and around Deepavali.

Asked about what more can be done to further accelerate the growth process amid risks of higher inflation and global uncertainty, Gupta called for more handholding to MSMEs and the agricultural sector by providing them relief from the untimely rains. From the State government perspective, he said that there are several key inputs which are controlled by States which  lead to industrial growth, land, labour, and power .

“The States should help industry to procure land at a reasonable price, that too in a very short time. Labour in the industrial clusters should be enhanced so that they get good housing, schools, etc, so that the labour mobility is improved,” he said while noting that the government is working very well on bringing new roads, new expressways, which improves connectivity. “They are also working on a good number of airports for improving connectivity, and they can increase more inland container depots for better connectivity to  the ports,” he said.

On the current economic situation, Gupta said that though it is doing well,  inflation has really become a big challenge. “This high inflation is the result of very high oil and gas prices, resulting in an all round increase in the  input costs for the various industries and  the transportation. Secondly, high inflation led by agriculture and other raw materials is see for agriculture,” he said. However, farmers and consumers are insulated from high prices.

title: Investor friendly taxation amid higher yield key to retaining FPI capital, says PHDCCI’s Gupta
